chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from one of his companions from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba from Abu al-Nu'man from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The one who does not prepare patience for the calamities of time will be frustrated.

key_terms.نَوَائِبِ الدَّهْرِ: Calamities or unexpected events of time/life
key_terms.يَعْجِزْ: Will be frustrated, become incapable, or fail

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of not preparing for the trials of life according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that patience is not merely a reactive virtue but a proactive spiritual discipline required to withstand the 'unexpected calamities' (nawā'ib) of destiny. Scholars highlight that the warning against being 'overwhelmed' (ya'jiz) implies that without pre-emptive cultivation of sabr, the soul lacks the resilience to process sudden trials, leading to spiritual collapse or loss of faith.
